Carl Lindner Jr. (Great American Insurance) was a co-investor. changes.new: Bob Castellini, a produce-distribution businessman (Castellini Company), led the January 2006 purchase of 70% of the club from Carl Lindner Jr. for $270M and ran it as principal owner for twenty years. MLB clubs approved the transfer of control to his son Phil Castellini, the club's president and CEO since July 2024, on February 12, 2026; Bob Castellini remains part of the ownership group. The Reds, an 1882 NL charter member, compete as a small-market club without significant payroll investment.
changes.fact: Corrects an earlier claim that Bob Castellini died in January 2024; he is alive, and control passed to Phil Castellini by MLB approval on February 12, 2026.

changes.new: Larry Dolan (media attorney, brother of Cablevision's Charles Dolan) bought the franchise in 2000 for $323M; his son Paul Dolan is the principal owner. David Blitzer, a Blackstone executive and multi-sport franchise investor, bought a 25% stake in June 2022 with an option to become controlling owner in 2028. Secondary reports in 2026 put his stake nearer 35%, which would be an increase on the 2022 purchase rather than a different deal; the 2028 path to control is the ownership transition point.
changes.fact: The June 2022 announcement was a 25% stake with an option for control in six years (2028). Later reports of ~35% are treated as an increase, not a conflicting figure.
